 Montgomery County District Court
 Cause No. 2024-CV-0049
 Donna Morris, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Defendant's Original Answer
Date:
6-27-24
Counsel for defendant:
Marilyn Fox, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defenadnt generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict
proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence, as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.
For further answer, and without assuming any burden of proof that the law places on Plaintiff, Defendant asserts the
following affirmative defenses.
First, Plaintiff's own negligence proximately caused or contributed to the collision alleged in the Petition. Plaintiff failed
to keep a proper lookout, failed to yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic, and failed to control the speed of the
vehicle under the circumstances. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery
must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and Plaintiff may be barred entirely if that percentage
exceeds fifty percent.
Second, Defendant invokes the proportionate responsibility provisions of Chapter 33 and requsets that the trier of fact
determine the percentage of responsibility of every responsible third party and settling person, as permitted by law.
Third, Defendant asserts that any damages claimed were caused by a preexisting or subsequent condition unrelated
to the collision, and that Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by pursuing reasonable medical treatment and returning
to available work.
</page>
